programme.desc: Doberman gives lady a ride on her chair; Sherman the spiderman kitten; bird tears up dollar bill and makes feathers; dog plays child's piano; man balances dog in his palm.

programme.title: Mishaps
programme.desc: Buddy climbs ladder; dog flips for water; baby in drawer; dog jumps onto cinder block several times.

programme.title: Chore Time
programme.desc: Dog leading another dog around with leash; Gizmo, the dog, gets mail; dog with bucket on his head.

programme.title: Tasty Treats
programme.desc: Squirrel taking nut from man's mouth; chicken steals cat food; parrot feeding dog.

programme.title: Eat, Drink And Be Merry
programme.desc: Feast on our food friendly countdown with kids underestimating the power of wasabi, cooking demonstration blunders and a boy’s abundant love of peanut butter.

programme.title: Go Play Outside
programme.desc: Whether the beach, a playground or your backyard, this countdown proves the best and funniest adventures happen outdoors.

programme.title: Caught On Clips

programme.title: Vacation Was Not Going As Planned

programme.title: The Learning Curve

programme.title: Cubicle

programme.title: Turin, Italy

Steven Rinella talks with paleontologist, evolutionary biologist, and author, Steve Brusatte.

programme.title: Wired To Hunt
programme.desc: What can 100+ farms teach us about big bucks? To answer it, Jake is joined by Jack Huston with Midwest Deer Surveys, who has flown hundreds of properties with thermal drones and seen exactly where deer are - and more importantly, where they aren’t. From density rings and social stress to bedding, pressure, and why “thicker” farms consistently produce, this episode challenges a lot of conventional thinking. We also get into how doe harvest impacts herds over time, what role genetics actually play, and why many hunters don’t struggle killing deer.

programme.title: A Cold Wind Is Blowing
programme.desc: Enjoy a chilling countdown of roof sledding fiascos, ski-less skiers and speed skating catastrophes in our hilarious snow-capped edition.

programme.title: Look What I Can Do
programme.desc: Doberman gives lady a ride on her chair; Sherman the spiderman kitten; bird tears up dollar bill and makes feathers; dog plays child's piano; man balances dog in his palm.

programme.title: Mishaps
programme.desc: Buddy climbs ladder; dog flips for water; baby in drawer; dog jumps onto cinder block several times.

programme.title: Chore Time
programme.desc: Dog leading another dog around with leash; Gizmo, the dog, gets mail; dog with bucket on his head.

programme.title: Tasty Treats
programme.desc: Squirrel taking nut from man's mouth; chicken steals cat food; parrot feeding dog.

programme.title: Eat, Drink And Be Merry
programme.desc: Feast on our food friendly countdown with kids underestimating the power of wasabi, cooking demonstration blunders and a boy’s abundant love of peanut butter.

programme.title: Go Play Outside
programme.desc: Whether the beach, a playground or your backyard, this countdown proves the best and funniest adventures happen outdoors.

programme.title: Caught On Clips
programme.desc: Don't miss the wildest, wackiest and most jaw-dropping videos from dangerous severe weather to heart-stopping close calls to adorable animal antics -- all caught on video.

programme.title: Vacation Was Not Going As Planned
programme.desc: Vacation misadventures make up the top spots on the countdown with a little girl gobbled by a big wave, zany zip line attempts, falling kites and a surprising game of cruise ship billiards.

programme.title: The Learning Curve
programme.desc: It takes trial and error for a girl doing her homework, a dog sitting at a table and a girl with her head stuck in a bannister to get past the learning curve.

programme.title: The Family Dynamic
programme.desc: A man pranking his son with a water bottle, children making a mess and a little boy cutting his sister’s hair are all caught on video.

programme.title: Fire and Ice
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau explores the cause of recent forest fires. We examine the nature of lightning strikes and how scientists are tracking them. We visit the country of Iceland and venture onto a large glacier and explore an ice cave. We also discover why glaciers are melting and how this will change the sea level

programme.title: Evolving Earth
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Utah where scientists have discovered a massive amount of dinosaur bones. We also go to an area where dinosaur footprints have been preserved. Then we visit Hawaii and see how these islands evolved from volcanoes. Philippe then tours an old coal mine in Pennsylvania and explores the fascinating way fossil fuels were formed.

programme.title: Invisible Impacts
programme.desc: Join host Nick Uhas and his guests as they shine a light on the unseen science behind our everyday lives. This week's experiments explore the resonant frequencies of bridges and human bodies.

programme.title: Cubicle
programme.desc: The Cubicle was originally designed to set workers free. A futuristic designer named Robert Propst dreamed up "The Action Office" as a groovy 1960s workplace utopia that would unleash the modern knowledge worker's vast untapped potential. This is how it all went so wrong.

programme.title: Turin, Italy
programme.desc: Lifelong photographer and journalist Jefferson Graham shows off the most photographable places through the lens of his smartphone. He also gives useful tips on how to get great phone vacation photos in fantastic places.

programme.title: Offline with Jon Favreau
programme.desc: In a world of little trust and big echo chambers, how do campaigns persuade voters that their candidates are worth voting for? With the midterms nearly upon us, Jon sits down with campaign expert Greta Carnes––who ran organizing for Pete Buttigieg’s presidential campaign and collaborates with Vote Save America––to discuss why the old campaign playbook is breaking down, what organizing looks like in a world of unanswered calls, ignored texts, and increasingly sophisticated technology, and how Democrats can actually build relationships with voters that last beyond Election Day.

programme.title: Pod Save America
programme.desc: CNN's Chief Data Analyst Harry Enten joins Tommy for one last deep dive ahead of Election Day. They break down the rising chance of a Democratic blowout in the House, how much to trust the polls, and what to watch for as results come in on Tuesday night. They also crunch the numbers on the most nail-biting Senate races and take a look at the most surprising states that are now in play. Then, Harry tells Tommy what it's like being Trump's favorite pollster.

programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.desc: Trump takes a long, hard look at John Husted, Kimberly Guilfoyle takes a bow from her ambassadorship, and new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia takes a few questions about her husband… we mean, the president! This week, former NASA astronaut Danny Olivas talks voting in America and farting in space, while Moshe Kosher squints hard enough to see the brighter side of life. The Rant Wheel takes us 360 through spacesuit underwear, AI-induced boredom, and America’s last movie star, Tom Cruise. And we turn the page to read a few Second Thoughts.

programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.desc: Gas prices go up, Ukraine’s Starlink goes down, and Ilhan Omar is caught in the middle.
